name: Parkinson's disease psychosis
aliases: Hallucinations and delusions in Parkinson's disease
summary: Pimavanserin, a selective 5-HT2A inverse agonist without dopamine-blocking activity, is the only FDA-labeled treatment for hallucinations and delusions associated with Parkinson's disease psychosis. Low-dose clozapine and quetiapine are used off-label; most other antipsychotics worsen motor symptoms.
plainSummary: Some people with Parkinson's disease begin to see or believe things that aren't real. One medicine is approved for this, and it does not make movement problems worse.

approved.indication: Treatment of hallucinations and delusions associated with Parkinson's disease psychosis.

dosing.notes: 10 mg once daily with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Avoid strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. No dose adjustment for renal or hepatic impairment. QT prolongation: avoid with other QT-prolonging drugs and in patients with known QT prolongation or arrhythmia history.

boxedWarnings: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis
contraindications: History of hypersensitivity reaction to pimavanserin or any component
approved.plainSummary: Pimavanserin is a once-a-day medicine that can reduce hallucinations and false beliefs in Parkinson's disease without worsening tremor or stiffness. It carries a warning about higher risk of death in older adults with dementia-related psychosis.

verified.note: Indication, dosing, CYP3A4 adjustments, boxed warning, and contraindication checked on the label revised 4/2026. QT warning wording is summarized from Warnings and Precautions and was not re-quoted. No 2024–2026 changes to the PDP indication were found.
